statement: The function returns a result r and r is the maximum length of an increasing path in matrix. Formally, a cell is a pair (i,j) with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. An increasing path of length k >= 1 is a sequence of cells (i_0,j_0),...,(i_{k-1},j_{k-1}) such that every listed cell is in bounds and, for every t with 0 <= t < k-1, |i_{t+1}-i_t| + |j_{t+1}-j_t| = 1 and matrix[i_t][j_t] < matrix[i_{t+1}][j_{t+1}]. Then r = max { k | there exists an increasing path of length k }.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix). The input is a valid problem matrix: m >= 1; let n = len(matrix[0]); 1 <= n <= 200; m <= 200; every row matrix[i] has length n; and 0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2147483647 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail) for every valid input.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix). The input is a valid problem matrix: m >= 1; let n = len(matrix[0]); 1 <= n <= 200; m <= 200; every row matrix[i] has length n; and 0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2147483647 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= m * n.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix). The input is a valid problem matrix: m >= 1; let n = len(matrix[0]); 1 <= n <= 200; m <= 200; every row matrix[i] has length n; and 0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2147483647 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists an increasing path in matrix of length r, where an increasing path of length k is a sequence of k in-bounds cells whose consecutive cells are orthogonally adjacent and whose matrix values are strictly increasing along the sequence.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix). The input is a valid problem matrix: m >= 1; let n = len(matrix[0]); 1 <= n <= 200; m <= 200; every row matrix[i] has length n; and 0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2147483647 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every increasing path in matrix has length at most r; equivalently, for every k such that there exists an increasing path of length k, k <= r.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix). The input is a valid problem matrix: m >= 1; let n = len(matrix[0]); 1 <= n <= 200; m <= 200; every row matrix[i] has length n; and 0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2147483647 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if matrix[i][j] = matrix[i'][j'] for every i,i',j,j' with 0 <= i < m, 0 <= i' < m, 0 <= j < n, and 0 <= j' < n.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix). The input is a valid problem matrix: m >= 1; let n = len(matrix[0]); 1 <= n <= 200; m <= 200; every row matrix[i] has length n; and 0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2147483647 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and m = 1, r is the maximum k >= 1 for which there exists an integer s with 0 <= s and s + k <= n such that either (for every t with 0 <= t < k-1, matrix[0][s+t] < matrix[0][s+t+1]) or (for every t with 0 <= t < k-1, matrix[0][s+t] > matrix[0][s+t+1]).
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix). The input is a valid problem matrix: m >= 1; let n = len(matrix[0]); 1 <= n <= 200; m <= 200; every row matrix[i] has length n; and 0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2147483647 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Also m = 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and n = 1, r is the maximum k >= 1 for which there exists an integer s with 0 <= s and s + k <= m such that either (for every t with 0 <= t < k-1, matrix[s+t][0] < matrix[s+t+1][0]) or (for every t with 0 <= t < k-1, matrix[s+t][0] > matrix[s+t+1][0]).
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix). The input is a valid problem matrix: m >= 1; let n = len(matrix[0]); 1 <= n <= 200; m <= 200; every row matrix[i] has length n; and 0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2147483647 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Also n = 1.

statement: Whenever longest_increasing_path(A) returns a result r and longest_increasing_path(B) returns a result s, r = s.
preconditions: Let A be a valid problem matrix with m = len(A) >= 1 and n = len(A[0]) satisfying 1 <= n <= 200, m <= 200, all rows of A have length n, and 0 <= A[i][j] <= 2147483647 for all cells. Let B be the n x m matrix defined by B[j][i] = A[i][j] for all i,j.

statement: Whenever longest_increasing_path(A) returns a result rA and longest_increasing_path(B) returns a result rB, rA = rB.
preconditions: Let A and B be valid problem matrices with the same dimensions m x n, where m = len(A) = len(B) >= 1, n = len(A[0]) = len(B[0]) with 1 <= n <= 200, m <= 200, all rows have length n, and all entries of A and B are between 0 and 2147483647. Assume that for every ordered pair of cells (i,j) and (i',j') with 0 <= i,i' < m, 0 <= j,j' < n, and |i-i'| + |j-j'| = 1, the inequality A[i][j] < A[i'][j'] holds if and only if B[i][j] < B[i'][j'] holds.

statement: Whenever longest_increasing_path(A) returns a result rA and longest_increasing_path(B) returns a result rB, rA >= rB.
preconditions: Let A be a valid problem matrix with m = len(A) >= 1 and n = len(A[0]) satisfying 1 <= n <= 200, m <= 200, all rows of A have length n, and 0 <= A[i][j] <= 2147483647 for all cells. Let r0,c0,mb,nb be integers with 0 <= r0, 0 <= c0, 1 <= mb, 1 <= nb, r0 + mb <= m, and c0 + nb <= n. Let B be the mb x nb matrix defined by B[i][j] = A[r0+i][c0+j] for 0 <= i < mb and 0 <= j < nb.

statement: Let D be the number of distinct integers appearing among the entries matrix[i][j] for 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= D.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix). The input is a valid problem matrix: m >= 1; let n = len(matrix[0]); 1 <= n <= 200; m <= 200; every row matrix[i] has length n; and 0 <= matrix[i][j] <= 2147483647 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.
